branches.description: Academy locations. Financial records are location-aware (invoices.location_id, payment_collections.branch_id), affecting invoice/payment filtering, invoice and credit-note numbering, and finance reporting.

columns.name: location_id
columns.description: References branches.id.

columns.name: last_number
columns.description: Last credit-note number issued for this branch.

credit_note_numbers.description: Operational metadata tracking the last credit-note number used per branch, mirroring invoice_numbers. A row here is not itself a credit note — actual credit notes live in invoices with the credit-note type.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: References students.id.

columns.name: balance
columns.description: Current account balance.

columns.name: net_payment
columns.description: Net payment amount contributing to the balance.

columns.name: net_invoice
columns.description: Net invoiced amount contributing to the balance.

columns.name: net_credit
columns.description: Net credit-note amount contributing to the balance.

customer_balances.description: Maintained current financial account position per customer (money, not service units — do not confuse with package_balances). This is a calculated summary, not the source ledger; the authoritative event/detail tables are invoices, payment_collections, payment_allocations, and customer_transactions.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: References students.id.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: References invoices.id, when this transaction relates to an invoice.

columns.name: payment_id
columns.description: References payment_collections.id, when this transaction relates to a payment.

columns.name: payment_allocation_id
columns.description: References payment_allocations.id, when this transaction relates to an allocation.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Kind of financial event this transaction represents.

customer_transactions.description: Financial transaction ledger for a customer — the best table for reconstructing a customer's chronological financial activity (invoices, payments, allocations, credit notes). For exact invoice/payment detail, join back to the underlying source table via invoice_id/payment_id/payment_allocation_id.

columns.name: status
columns.description: 0=Open, 1=Callback, 2=Assessment, 3=Converted, 4=Dead end, 5=Assessment Report, 6=In Renewal, 7=Renewed, 8=Scheduled, 9=Other.

follow_ups.description: Sales/renewal follow-up activity for a student — tracks the lead/renewal pipeline, not academic or financial data.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: References invoices.id.

columns.name: type
columns.description: When set to "package", this line represents a package/service purchase or return; value then holds the service/package identifier.

columns.name: value
columns.description: For package-type items, the related service/package identifier.

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Units purchased or returned (credit-note items can reduce package purchases).

invoice_items.description: Individual line items belonging to an invoice or credit note (tutoring, lesson packages, registration charges, other services). Use this table for "what was this invoice for" questions rather than inferring from the invoice header alone.

columns.name: last_number
columns.description: Last invoice number issued for this branch.

columns.name: location_id
columns.description: References branches.id — numbering sequences are branch-scoped.

invoice_numbers.description: Operational metadata for safely generating sequential, branch-aware invoice numbers (avoids unsafe MAX(invoice_number)+1 under concurrent creation). Do not use when computing revenue, receivables, or customer balances.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: References students.id — the customer is the student, even though parents/relatives may receive/pay the invoice.

columns.name: total
columns.description: Original total value of the invoice.

columns.name: status
columns.description: 0=awaiting approval, 1=awaiting payment/allocation (meaning depends on type), 2=paid, 3=void. Voided invoices are not active receivables.

columns.name: type
columns.description: Distinguishes a normal invoice from a credit note.

columns.name: outstanding
columns.description: Remaining amount to be settled: total - allocated amount.

columns.name: total_paid
columns.description: How much money or credit has been allocated against the invoice.

columns.name: location_id
columns.description: References branches.id.

invoices.description: Master financial-document table. A row is either a normal invoice (increases amount owed) or a credit note (reduces/reverses a prior charge), distinguished by type. status: 0=awaiting approval, 1=awaiting payment (invoice) or awaiting allocation (credit note), 2=paid, 3=void. outstanding = total - allocated amount. Do not sum invoices.total to answer "how much does a customer owe" — use status/type plus payments/allocations.

columns.name: service_id
columns.description: References services.id.

columns.name: student_id
columns.description: References students.id.

columns.name: status
columns.description: 0=scheduled, 1=cancelled, 2=attended, 3=missed. Attended and missed both count toward package usage; scheduled affects scheduled quantities only.

lesson_and_events.description: Not an accounting table itself, but directly drives package accounting: attended/missed lessons count toward package usage, scheduled lessons affect scheduled quantities. status: 0=scheduled, 1=cancelled, 2=attended, 3=missed.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: References students.id.

columns.name: service_id
columns.description: References services.id.

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: What caused this balance change (see description for possible values).

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: References invoices.id, when the event originated from an invoice.

columns.name: invoice_item_id
columns.description: References invoice_items.id, when the event originated from a specific line item.

columns.name: lesson_and_event_id
columns.description: References lesson_and_events.id, when the event originated from lesson usage.

columns.name: purchased_delta
columns.description: Change in purchased units from this event.

columns.name: used_delta
columns.description: Change in used units from this event.

columns.name: scheduled_delta
columns.description: Change in scheduled units from this event.

columns.name: balance_delta
columns.description: Change in balance from this event.

columns.name: purchased_after
columns.description: Resulting purchased total after this event.

columns.name: used_after
columns.description: Resulting used total after this event.

columns.name: scheduled_after
columns.description: Resulting scheduled total after this event.

columns.name: balance_after
columns.description: Resulting balance after this event.

package_balance_ledger.description: Event/audit ledger explaining why a package_balances row changed (package_balances gives current state; this table explains the history). event_type values include invoice_purchase, credit_note_return, lesson_used, lesson_usage_reversed, package_balance_recomputed. Particularly valuable for AI explanations and auditing package balance changes.

columns.name: service_id
columns.description: References services.id.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: References students.id.

columns.name: purchased
columns.description: Total units acquired through qualifying invoice items.

columns.name: scheduled
columns.description: Units scheduled as lessons/events but not yet consumed.

columns.name: used
columns.description: Units consumed through attended or missed lessons/events.

columns.name: balance
columns.description: Remaining available units: purchased - used.

columns.name: last_invoice_id
columns.description: Last invoice involved in updating this package position.

package_balances.description: Current lesson/service unit balance purchased by a customer (educational/service units, not money — do not confuse with customer_balances). balance = purchased - used, with scheduled tracked separately. Sourced from invoice_items + invoices (purchases/returns/voids) and lesson_and_events (usage).

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: References invoices.id.

columns.name: payment_id
columns.description: References payment_collections.id.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Amount of this payment allocated to this specific invoice.

payment_allocations.description: Connects payments to invoices, solving the many-to-many nature of settlement: one payment can settle several invoices, and one invoice can be paid by several payments. Never assume a payment paid a particular invoice just because they share a customer_id — only an allocation row proves it. Deleting an allocation must restore the allocated value to the invoice outstanding amount, not just delete a row.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: References students.id.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Total amount received in this payment.

columns.name: balance
columns.description: Portion of this payment not yet allocated to any invoice.

columns.name: method
columns.description: Payment method key, matching payment_methods.method — fixed set of values (cash, cheque, credit_card, debit_card, direct_debit, ach, bank_transfer, e_transfer, paypal, venmo, cc_avenue, other). Never guess a value outside this list; you can filter directly on this column without joining payment_methods. "Card" without further detail means credit_card + debit_card + cc_avenue combined.

columns.name: branch_id
columns.description: References branches.id.

payment_collections.description: Actual payments received from customers — the primary payment-receipt table. A payment does not necessarily map 1:1 to an invoice; a payment can exist before its full value is allocated (balance = amount - allocated so far, available for future allocation). For "how much money did we receive", query this table, not invoices.

columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: References invoices.id.

columns.name: amount
columns.description: Amount recorded in this history entry.

columns.name: allocation_id
columns.description: References payment_allocations.id — join through this to reach the payment_collections row.

payment_histories.description: Historical/audit record of how a payment was allocated to an invoice. Complements payment_allocations (which reflects the current allocation state) with a history/audit trail. Prefer this table when explaining how an invoice arrived at its current paid state, rather than only reading the current outstanding value. Note: there is no payment_id column here — the link to the payment is via allocation_id -> payment_allocations.payment_id.

columns.name: method
columns.description: Machine key for the payment method — see the table description for the fixed list of valid values.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Display name of the payment method.

payment_methods.description: Payment options available to the organisation, referenced by payment_collections.method. Fixed set of values (method -> name): cash->Cash, cheque->Cheque, credit_card->Credit Card, debit_card->Debit Card, direct_debit->Direct Debit, ach->ACH, bank_transfer->Bank Transfer, e_transfer->E-Transfer, paypal->PayPal, venmo->Venmo, cc_avenue->CC Avenue, other->Others. Never guess or invent a method value outside this list. When a question says "card" without specifying which kind, it means credit_card + debit_card + cc_avenue combined (CC Avenue is a payment gateway used for card processing) — filter with method IN ('credit_card', 'debit_card', 'cc_avenue'), not a LIKE/equality match on the word "card".

services.description: Educational/service products that can be purchased, particularly important for package invoice items — connects the invoicing/payment system to the operational learning product being sold (see package_balances.service_id, package_balance_ledger.service_id).

columns.name: status
columns.description: 0=Inactive, 1=Active, 2=Prospective, 3=Pause.

students.description: Students are treated as the customer/account entity throughout the invoicing subsystem — "customer", "student", and "learner account" typically refer to the same financial entity, even though parents/relatives may be the ones who pay or receive notifications.

examples.invoice_lifecycle: Typical flow: create invoice -> add invoice_items -> calculate subtotal/tax/total -> allocate invoice_number -> await approval -> await payment -> receive payment -> create payment_allocation -> update invoice outstanding/total_paid -> update customer_balances -> add customer_transactions row -> invoice becomes paid once outstanding reaches 0. A credit note follows the same document structure but reverses/reduces charges rather than adding them.
examples.payment_lifecycle: Customer pays 1,000 -> a payment_collections row is created (linked to payment method, customer, branch) -> one or more payment_allocations rows split it across invoices -> matching payment_histories rows record the allocation -> a customer_transactions row is added -> customer_balances is recalculated.
examples.partial_payment: Invoice total = 1,000. Payment 1 of 400 is allocated: total_paid becomes 400, outstanding becomes 600, status stays awaiting payment. Payment 2 of 600 is allocated: total_paid becomes 1,000, outstanding becomes 0, status becomes paid (2).
examples.payment_split_across_invoices: A single payment of 2,000 can be allocated as: Invoice 101 -> 500, Invoice 102 -> 700, Invoice 103 -> 300 (total allocated 1,500), leaving payment_collections.balance = 500 still available for a future allocation to another invoice.
examples.package_balance_ledger_walkthrough: package_balances.balance = 12 only tells you the current state. package_balance_ledger can explain how it got there, e.g.: +20 purchased_delta from an invoice_purchase event (Invoice 101), -2 used_delta from a lesson_used event (Lesson 501), -2 used_delta from another lesson_used event (Lesson 534), -4 balance change from a credit_note_return event (Credit Note 205) => 12 remaining. Prefer this table over package_balances when a question asks "why" a balance changed rather than just "what" it currently is.
ai_rules: An invoice is money requested/receivable; a payment is money received. Do not treat invoice totals as payment receipts.
Never infer that a payment settled a specific invoice just because they share a customer_id — only payment_allocations/payment_histories rows prove settlement.
Credit notes reduce or reverse charges and must be included in balance calculations, not ignored.
Voided invoices (status=3) are not active receivables and should be excluded from outstanding-balance calculations.
customer_balances is money; package_balances is educational/service units. Do not conflate the two when a question could mean either.

When a question asks why a value changed, prefer ledger/history tables (customer_transactions, payment_histories, package_balance_ledger) over current-state summary tables (customer_balances, package_balances, invoices.outstanding).
